title: Bounded-error probabilistic decision in time
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $L$ be a language of Boolean strings, and let $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. The machine decides $L$ with bounded error within time $T$ if, on every input $x$, it halts within $T(|x|)$ steps and its output equals the indicator of membership in $L$ with probability at least $2/3$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Booleans
$L$ is a language of Boolean strings
$T$ maps natural numbers to natural numbers
The correct membership-indicator output occurs with probability at least $2/3$
